q.t: A tangent to a circle is ___ to the radius at the point of contact.
q.e: The radius is the shortest path from the centre to the tangent line, and the shortest path to a line is perpendicular.

q.t: How many tangents can be drawn to a circle from a point outside it?
q.e: One touching on each side of the circle.

q.t: A point is 5 cm from the centre of a circle of radius 3 cm. Find the length of the tangent from it.
q.e: Radius ⊥ tangent makes a right triangle: √(25 − 9).

q.t: The two tangents from an outside point to a circle are…
q.e: The two right triangles share the hypotenuse and have equal radii, so they are congruent (RHS).

q.t: How many tangents can be drawn at one point on a circle?
q.e: Only one line is perpendicular to the radius at that point.

q.t: A point is 13 cm from the centre and its tangent is 12 cm long. Find the radius.
Find the angle between a tangent and the radius at the point of contact (in degrees).
q.e: A tangent is always perpendicular to the radius there.

q.t: Tangents drawn at the two ends of a diameter are…
q.e: Both are perpendicular to the same diameter.

q.t: A line meeting a circle at two points is called a…
q.e: A chord is only the part inside; the full line is a secant. A tangent meets the circle once.

q.t: How many tangents can be drawn from a point inside a circle?
q.e: Every line through an inside point cuts the circle twice.

q.t: TP and TQ are tangents from T to a circle with centre O. ∠PTQ = 70°. Find ∠POQ.
q.e: In quadrilateral OPTQ the angles at P and Q are 90°, so ∠POQ = 360° − 180° − 70°.

q.t: Quadrilateral ABCD is drawn round a circle with AB = 6, BC = 7 and CD = 4 cm. Find AD.
q.e: Equal tangents from each corner give AB + CD = BC + AD.

q.t: A point is 17 cm from the centre of a circle of radius 8 cm. Find the tangent length.
Two concentric circles have radii 5 cm and 3 cm. Find the length of a chord of the larger that touches the smaller.
q.e: The radius to the touching point bisects the chord at right angles: half-chord = √(25 − 9) = 4.

q.t: PA and PB are tangents from P to a circle with centre O and radius 5 cm. ∠APB = 60°. Find PA.
q.e: OP bisects ∠APB, so ∠APO = 30° and tan 30° = OA/PA = 5/PA.

q.t: PA and PB are tangents from P to a circle with centre O. ∠APB = 80°. Find ∠OAB.
The incircle of ΔABC touches the sides at D, E, F, with AF = 4, BD = 6 and CE = 5 cm. Find the perimeter.
q.e: Each tangent length appears twice (AF = AE, BD = BF, CE = CD).

q.t: A tangent from a point 25 cm from the centre is 24 cm long. Find the radius.
A parallelogram drawn round a circle must be a…
o: kite that is not a rhombus
q.e: AB + CD = BC + AD, and opposite sides are equal, so 2AB = 2BC.

q.t: A chord 8 cm long is in a circle of radius 5 cm. How far is it from the centre?
q.e: The perpendicular from the centre halves the chord: √(25 − 16).

q.t: PQ is a 24 cm chord of a circle of radius 13 cm. The tangents at P and Q meet at T. Find TP.
q.e: OR ⊥ PQ with OR = 5. In right ΔOPT, the triangles OPT and ORP are similar, so TP/OP = PR/OR: TP = 13 × 12/5.

q.t: Two tangents PA and PB from P to a circle make ∠APB = 120°. Then OP equals…
q.e: ∠APO = 60°, so cos 60° = AP/OP = 1/2.

q.t: A quadrilateral is drawn round a circle with sides AB = x + 3, BC = 2x, CD = x + 4, DA = 2x − 1. Find x.
q.e: AB + CD = BC + DA: 2x + 7 = 4x − 1.

q.t: A circle is inscribed in a right triangle with legs 6 cm and 8 cm. Find its radius.
q.e: The hypotenuse is 10. In a right triangle r = (a + b − c)/2, since the tangents from the right-angle corner equal r.

q.t: The two tangents from P to a circle of radius 6 cm are at right angles. Find the length of each tangent.
q.e: OAPB has three right angles, so it is a rectangle with OA = OB — a square.

q.t: AB is a diameter of a circle with centre O and ∠BAC = 30° for a chord AC. The tangent at C meets AB extended at D. Then BC equals…
q.e: ∠ACB = 90° (semicircle), so ∠ABC = 60°. OA = OC gives ∠OCA = 30°, so ∠OCB = 60°; OC ⊥ CD makes ∠BCD = 30°. Then ∠BDC = 60° − 30° = 30°, so ΔBCD is isosceles.

q.t: TP and TQ are tangents to a circle with centre O and ∠PTQ = 50°. Find ∠OPQ.
Two concentric circles have radii 13 cm and 5 cm. Find the chord of the larger that touches the smaller.
A circle touches all four sides of ABCD with AB = 10, BC = 12 and CD = 9 cm. Find AD.
q.e: AB + CD = BC + AD.

q.t: From an outside point P, the tangent PT is 12 cm and the nearest point of the circle is 8 cm from P. Find the radius.
q.e: OP = r + 8 and (r + 8)² = r² + 144, so 16r = 80.

q.t: A circle of radius 2 cm is inscribed in ΔABC, touching BC at D with BD = 4 cm and DC = 6 cm. Find AB + AC.
q.e: Let the tangent from A be x. s = 10 + x. Area = r × s = 2(10 + x) and also √(s × x × 4 × 6). Equating gives x = 2, so AB = 6, AC = 8.

q.t: Two concentric circles have radii 5 cm and 3 cm. Chord AB of the larger touches the smaller at P; AD is a diameter of the larger. Find BD.
q.e: O and P are midpoints of AD and AB, so OP is half of BD (midpoint theorem). OP = 3.

q.t: ΔABC has AB = 12, BC = 8 and CA = 10 cm. Its incircle touches AB at F. Find AF.
q.e: Tangent from A = s − (side opposite A) = 15 − 8.

q.t: A circle is inscribed in a right triangle with legs 9 cm and 40 cm. Find its radius.
q.e: The hypotenuse is 41, and r = (9 + 40 − 41)/2.

q.t: PA and PB are tangents from P, with PA = 10 cm. A third tangent at a point C on the minor arc AB meets PA at D and PB at E. Find the perimeter of ΔPDE.
q.e: DC = DA and EC = EB, so PD + DE + PE = PA + PB.

q.t: TP and TQ are tangents from T to a circle with centre O. ∠PTQ equals…
q.e: ∠TPQ = 90° − ∠PTQ/2 and ∠OPQ = 90° − ∠TPQ = ∠PTQ/2.

q.t: A circle touches BC at P and the extensions of AB and AC at Q and R. AB = 7, BC = 8 and CA = 9 cm. Find AQ.
q.e: BQ = BP and CR = CP, so AQ + AR = AB + BC + CA = 24. AQ = AR = 12.

q.t: A circle is inscribed in quadrilateral ABCD with ∠D = 90°. BC = 30 cm, CD = 20 cm and the tangent from B is 18 cm. Find the radius.
q.e: Tangent from C = 30 − 18 = 12, so the tangent from D = 20 − 12 = 8. With ∠D = 90° the radii and tangents at D form a square.

q.t: PA and PB are tangents from P with ∠APB = 60° and PA = 7 cm. Find AB.
q.e: PA = PB and the angle between is 60°, so ΔPAB is equilateral.

q.t: A circle has radius 5 cm and P is 13 cm from its centre O. Tangents touch at A and B. Find the area of quadrilateral OAPB.
q.e: PA = 12. OAPB is two right triangles of area ½ × 5 × 12.
